name: Ancient Villages of Northern Syria
description: In the limestone hills of northwestern Syria, between Aleppo and Idlib, some 40 villages sit abandoned in eight archaeological parks. Built between the 1st and 7th centuries and left empty by about the 10th, they still show houses, churches, pagan temples, bathhouses and water cisterns in weathered stone. Walking among them, you can see how farming communities lived as Roman paganism gave way to Byzantine Christianity.
